ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a two-transistor current mirror. Q1 on the left has its collector tied to its base, making it diode-connected, and this node is fed from the +24 V top rail through a 2.7 kΩ resistor. Q1 and Q2 share a common base connection, and their emitters are tied together to the lower rail. Q2 on the right has its collector connected through R_load, labeled 1.5 kΩ, to the +24 V rail. Reasoning: For a silicon transistor, the base-emitter drop is approximately 0.7 V. Since Q1's emitter is on the lower rail, the Q1 base/collector node is about 0.7 V above the lower rail. Therefore the voltage across the 2.7 kΩ reference resistor is approximately 24 V - 0.7 V = 23.3 V. The reference current is I_ref = 23.3 V / 2.7 kΩ = 0.00863 A ≈ 8.63 mA. By current mirror action, Q2 tries to maintain approximately the same current through R_load, so the approximate load current is 8.6 mA.
